chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, concerning wudu (ablution).
He said: When the water touches your skin, that is sufficient for you.

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the purifying substance in the ruling
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing discussed in the report
key_terms.جِلْدَكَ: your skin, the part of the body that water must reach
key_terms.فَحَسْبُكَ: it is sufficient for you, indicating legal adequacy
key_terms.مَسَّ: touched or reached, indicating direct contact

ai.seo_question: What amount of water is sufficient in wudu (ablution) and ghusl al-janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a concise legal ruling about ritual washing, indicating that the essential requirement is for water to reach the skin. In the chapter context, it relates to the amount of water sufficient for ghusl al-janabah and wudu (ablution), emphasizing adequacy rather than excess.
